Ships 15 seed routes plus a 20-entry candidate pool covering 7 target kinds (GitHub raw/codeload/main, npm registry, PyPI index, HuggingFace, general). Routes are verified before use: upstream IP lists go through a TLS handshake with full certificate-chain validation (a bare TCP check can be answered locally and report dead IPs as healthy), and failures advance a cooldown ladder of 2/5/15 minutes with the fastest healthy route picked per target kind. Routes are applied by rewriting the URL with one of four rules (prefix, registry, index, host-replace), reaching git, pip, npm, pnpm, gh, curl and wget through three paths: the shell seam (download commands the model runs through the bash tool are intercepted and rewritten automatically; commands wrapped by the pwsh tool, and fetches made by the host itself or the renderer, are not covered), two registered tools the model can call directly (line_pool_status, line_pool_run), and child-process spawn. Multi-line commands keep their line breaks and only the download segment is touched. URLs carrying credentials (user:token@host) are never rewritten, so tokens are not forwarded to third-party mirrors. No global config is modified. A sidebar panel lists every route with latency, failure reason and cooldown countdown, supports per-route retest and enable/disable, and shows live TUN/proxy status from network-adapter and loopback port checks. The candidate pool is re-verified every 24 hours so newly usable routes are added and dead ones dropped. 570 tests, 87% line coverage.

Computers run inside the authority and are handed only their own hand, the public record and the seat counts, so no hand can leak; the authority is the only place that decides which card ids leave it. Computers are driven by the room itself, so a one-person table keeps playing with nobody else on the LAN port. Humans have no turn timer, the collapsed floating pill can be dragged around the screen, and 179 unit tests pin the rules, the wire format, the theme tokens, the drag gesture, the history grouping and the computer seats.

She also remembers you between sessions: three fat-calls today and she greets you cold, three nickname-calls and she greets you warm, coming back after half an hour earns "I was not waiting for you", and the first few meetings she is shy - so the counters reset each local midnight and are stored in a state file the plugin owns. After ten quiet minutes she drifts to a corner, which is visual only and never moves the position you chose. The eight PNGs are bundled with the plugin and served by the plugin itself, so there are no third-party requests. NOTE - the artwork carries an OleapCrow mark and was supplied by the repository owner, the eight skins are recolourings of that one drawing, and the plugin has not been installed against a live DSH host.

Ships five reading themes (day, eye, sepia, dark, black) that follow the same settings file, and the panel is fully localized in Chinese and English. Reads the novel-reader data directory (on Windows %APPDATA%\novel-reader); macOS and Linux are supported too.

name: Stellum-Waq/dsh-pet-ronaldo
description: Cristiano Ronaldo desktop pet for DeepSeek Harness: a chibi Portugal number 7 mascot in a bottom-right overlay whose animation follows the agent state 鈥?dribbling while tools run, thinking during a turn, waiting at approvals, diving on errors 鈥?and jumping in a SIU celebration with a host-process sound when a turn completes; it can be dragged, looks at the cursor on hover, dives on a triple click, and a settings panel manages several pets and imports custom spritesheets. It also runs as a borderless, always-on-top native Windows window that keeps living after the browser is closed: hovering shows the current workspace and conversation title, double-clicking opens the Harness page in Edge, and dragging, mouse-wheel resizing and a right-click menu work there too, sharing position, size and behaviour with the web panel. Pet sheets may use any cell resolution and scale preserving aspect ratio (atlas.scaling: smooth | pixelated). v2.2 adds a video route 鈥?feed it a clip (green screen or ordinary footage) and its real motion becomes the pet animations, via automatic backdrop sampling, chroma keying with spill suppression, motion-based segment splitting and union-bbox alignment; already-extracted PNG frames work too, with no video decoder installed, and the clip audio can be cut into per-action sounds. Pets can also be published to the community gallery under the DPSL-1.0 sharing declaration, and installed from it in one click. v2.3 adapts it to DSH 0.2 desktop clients 鈥?the celebration sound now falls back to spawning PowerShell when the host no longer provides the shell service 鈥?and makes a single click play a short, configurable taunt animation (`interactions.clickAnim`).
